text: Morning. I'm restoring a 1950s 22-foot wooden sloop called the Sparrowhawk for a client's spring launch, so I'll want help planning the work.
Happy to help. What stage is she at?
Stripped to the frames. The ribs are mostly sound but I'll have to replace a few, and I prefer steam-bent oak ribs over laminated ones when the original used solid timber.
Understood. I'll keep that in mind. Laminated ribs are usually easier to get right.
No, that's not how I work, and don't tell me what's easier. Also I'd rather close a seam with cotton and linseed putty than a modern sealant.
Please be blunt with me. I don't want reassurance, I want the answer first and the reasons after it.
Noted: answer first, reasons after, no reassurance.
One more thing about how I like my notes: short numbered steps, not paragraphs.
The client launches the last Saturday of April, so the hull has to be tight by mid-April. No fibreglass over the planks, the lines stay original.
I'll bring the garboard plank template to the yard meeting this Friday, so I need the lofting notes ready before then.
Friday it is. I'll help you get the lofting notes ready.
I still can't tell whether the rot at the stem is only in the outer layer or runs into the stem itself, and I haven't found a way to settle it.
Salvaged bronze fittings go back on wherever they're sound, the budget is fixed.
